Application construction-sequence statements conflict (Tremval-to-Arpin vs. Columbia-to-Arpin then west to Tremval).

unresolved: Hypothesis part 1 (Tremval convergence): SUPPORTED for the NSPW-owned Grid Forward segment, not the ATC portion. Grid Forward segment 1N exits the Tremval Substation Expansion North (authorized); WWTC decision 5-CE-158 authorized the Tremval North site; Dairyland's 1515-CE-103 decision says Alma–Blair terminates at the new Tremval North Substation/switching station approved in 5-CE-158; Xcel names it Larkin Valley, ~0.5 mi north of the existing Tremval Substation near Blair. The link is a chain across documents, and Xcel's info sheet says Larkin Valley is 'near' (not 'formerly') Tremval North.

Hypothesis part 2 (both publish 2026–27 construction windows): NOT CONFIRMED as stated. Dairyland's page shows construction 2026–2027 (PSC decision: begin Q4 2026, in-service Sept 2028). Grid Forward publishes a project-wide Q4 2026 start with completion December 2030, not a 2026–27 window; for the Tremval-end NSPW segment, Xcel shows pre-construction ground activities 2026–2027 and general construction 2027–2030, and NSPW's Q2 2026 report moved its construction start to Q4 2027. Overlap with Alma–Blair general construction is therefore at most possible in 2027 (latest NSPW claim: Q4 2027), plus pre-construction overlap in 2026–27.

Hypothesis part 3 (shared-resource plans): CONFIRMED that the cited sources do not establish Dairyland–ATC (or Dairyland–NSPW) shared crews, equipment, laydown yards or schedules. The only documented statement is ATC's planning-level 'cooperatively working on plans' among ATC, Xcel and Dairyland. Note the Tremval-end work belongs to NSPW (Xcel), not ATC. Status is not-found-in-sources, not 'uncoordinated'.

Umbrella id 'atc-nspw-grid-forward' not used: sources clearly split the project into owner-specific packages (ATC PCO–Arpin–Columbia; NSPW, with WPPI/SMMPA co-owners, Tremval–PCO), each with its own construction responsibility, schedule claim and quarterly report. Modeled as grid-forward-atc and grid-forward-nspw.
NSPW construction-start claims conflict: Q4 2026 (final decision project-wide; NSPW Q1 2026 report) vs Q4 2027 (NSPW Q2 2026 report). The reason for the slip is not stated.

ATC construction status conflict: ATC Q2 2026 report says line construction began Q2 2026, but ATC's own website timeline graphic (image only, unverifiable as text) shows pre-construction 2026–2027 and general construction 2027–2030.
In-service conflict inside the final decision: 'completion by December 2030' (p54) vs '2029 dollars, the projected in-service year' (p53). All other sources say December 2030 or 2030.
No source gives a construction end date distinct from completion/in-service; all construction-window ends are upper bounds from completion or in-service statements.

Application construction-sequence statements conflict: p38 (printed 26) 'from Columbia to Aprin and from Tremval to Aprin' vs p42 (printed 30) 'from the Columbia Substation northward to the Arpin Substation and then west towards the Tremval Substation'.

The Xcel 'Golden Spike' end point (~3 mi south of Neillsville; segment ~39.25 mi) is not explicitly equated with the application's PCO (~1,400 ft west of Sherwood Rd & River Ave, which geocodes ~6.7 mi south of Neillsville's centroid). The PCO coordinate is the road intersection, not the offset point.
Larkin Valley Substation (new) is not in OSM; placed at Blair locality (5 km uncertainty). The existing Tremval Substation (OSM way 258582476) is ~1.7 km west of that centroid.

Green Lake Substation and 7 Mile Creek Substation could not be found by name in OSM; the ATC schematic route omits them (uses Wautoma -> North Randolph -> Wyocena), so it runs west of the actual Green Lake leg.
Final decision Certificate paragraph (p57) lists segments '1, 2, 3, ...' without 1N, while the Authorized Project Route paragraph (p36) lists '1N (C1N)'; treated as authorizing 1N.
Application lists existing Dairyland (DPC) taps (Badger Sands, Hixton, May Coulee) on the rebuilt NSPW W3401 line; whether Dairyland is coordinating on that work is not documented.

Columbia Substation (ATC endpoint) also appears in MISO BECI materials (miso-beci-scope-2025 p27) with separate substation modification work; that relation was not modeled here and needs a BECI project id and verification.

An ATC-only total cost is not stated as a single figure (itemized ATC costs appear in the final decision cost table, p53–54); only the NSPW segment total ($239,888,000) and whole-project total ($1,595,917,000) are sourced.
ATC and Xcel project web pages are undated; retrieval date 2026-09-26.
